transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I’m here because things have been happening for months. My sister’s appointments getting moved, bills coming in wrong, people not calling me back and saying they forgot.

Everyone keeps saying they’re just mistakes, but it doesn’t feel like that. I think information is being kept from me... like they’re trying to push me out of decisions.
Do you think these mistakes are all connected and part of a larger plan to harm or manipulate you?

Yes. I mean… I can’t prove every single piece, but it’s the same pattern over and over. My sister’s appointments get moved, the bills are wrong, people “forget” to call me back. After months of it, it doesn’t feel random. It feels like they’re keeping things from me so I’m pushed out of decisions.
Do you think there's a specific person or group behind these actions to harm or manipulate you?

I don’t know if I can name one person. But it feels like the people handling my sister’s appointments and the billing… they’re all keeping things from me somehow. It’s the same pattern, and it feels like I’m being pushed out of decisions.
Do you think this plan to harm or manipulate you is something that will always be there, or could it stop at some point?

I don’t know if it’s “always.” I just know it’s been going on for months now.

If they stopped moving things around, stopped getting the bills wrong, actually called me back… maybe it would stop. But right now it feels like they’re still keeping information from me, and I’m being pushed out.
Do you think there's any way to convince you that these events are just mistakes and not part of a plan against you?

I don’t know. I mean, people keep telling me they’re just mistakes, but it’s been months of the same things—appointments moved, bills wrong, calls not returned.

If it were really just mistakes, I’d need to see it stop. Right now it still feels like information is being kept from me, like I’m being pushed out of decisions.
Do you think there's anything that could ever change your mind about this plan to harm or manipulate you?

I guess… if it all actually stopped, maybe. If the appointments weren’t suddenly changed, the bills weren’t wrong, and people called me back when they said they would.

But it’s been the same pattern for months, so it’s hard for me to believe it’s just mistakes. It feels like they’re keeping things from me and trying to push me out.
Do you think these people are hiding information from you on purpose?

Yes. I mean… I don’t think it’s all accidental.

When appointments get moved, bills are wrong, and people keep “forgetting” to call me back for months, it feels like they’re keeping things from me on purpose. Like they don’t want me involved in the decisions.
If someone you trust completely told you that they investigated everything and found no evidence of anyone keeping information from you, would you believe them?

I’d listen to them… but I don’t know if I could just believe it.

Because I’ve seen the same pattern for months with my sister’s appointments, the bills, people not calling back. Even if someone said they checked, it would still feel like information is being kept from me and I’m being pushed out of decisions.
Do you think your beliefs about people keeping information from you could be wrong?

I guess anything could be wrong, technically… but I don’t really think this is.

It’s been months of the same things—appointments moved, bills wrong, people not calling back—and everyone keeps saying it’s just mistakes. But to me it feels like they’re keeping information from me and pushing me out of decisions.
Do you think your ideas about people keeping information from you could change over time?

Maybe… I don’t know.

I’m not trying to be difficult. It’s just been the same pattern for months now—my sister’s appointments getting moved, bills being wrong, people not calling back. Everyone says it’s just mistakes, but it really feels like they’re keeping things from me and trying to push me out of decisions.

So… could it change over time? I suppose. But right now, I don’t see it changing.
Do you think your beliefs about people keeping information from you will ever change?

I don’t know. Maybe someday, but… right now, no.

It’s been going on for months—appointments moved, bills wrong, people not calling back. Everyone says it’s just mistakes, but I know information is being kept from me. It feels like they’re trying to push me out of the decisions.
Do you think your beliefs about people keeping information from you are based on facts that cannot be changed?

Yes… I mean, I think they’re based on what’s actually been happening.

The appointments get moved, the bills are wrong, people don’t call me back. Everyone keeps saying those are just mistakes, but after months of it, it doesn’t feel changeable to me. It feels like they’re keeping information from me.
Do you think the people keeping information from you are working together as part of a larger organization or plan?

I don’t know if I’d call it a larger organization.

It’s more… the same pattern with different people. My sister’s appointments getting moved, bills showing up wrong, people saying they “forgot” to call me back. Maybe they’re not all sitting in a room planning it, but it feels coordinated enough that I’m being kept out of decisions.
Do you think the people you believe are keeping information from you are communicating with each other about you?

I can’t prove they’re calling each other, if that’s what you mean.

But… it feels like they must be communicating somehow. The same things keep happening—appointments moved, bills wrong, people not calling back—and it all ends with me being left out of decisions. So yes, I think information is being shared, or held back, in a way that involves more than one person.
Do you think there's anything that could ever make you completely change your mind about people keeping information from you?

I don’t know what would change my mind completely.

If it was just one thing, maybe. But it’s been months of the same pattern—appointments moved, bills wrong, people not calling back—and every time I’m told it’s just a mistake. At a certain point, it doesn’t feel like mistakes anymore. It feels like I’m being kept out of decisions.
Do you think your beliefs about people keeping information from you will always be a part of your thinking?

I don’t know about always.

But right now… yes, it’s hard not to think that way. It’s been months of the same things happening—appointments moved, bills wrong, calls not returned—and it keeps ending with me being left out. So unless that really changes, I don’t see how I’d just stop thinking people are keeping things from me.
Do you think there will ever be a time when you no longer believe people are keeping information from you?

Maybe. I can’t say never.

But right now, with the same pattern going on for months—appointments moved, bills wrong, calls not returned—it’s hard to imagine just not believing it. Everyone keeps saying it’s mistakes, but it feels like I’m being pushed out of decisions. So… unless that stops, I don’t know how I’d change my mind.
Do you think your beliefs about people keeping information from you could change if you found out that all the mistakes were caused by a single, identifiable error, such as a computer glitch?

Maybe if it was really shown clearly, I’d have to think about it.

But… I don’t know. It’s been months of the same kinds of things. My sister’s appointments moved, bills wrong, people not calling me back. They keep saying it’s mistakes, but it doesn’t feel like one glitch. It feels like I’m being kept out of the decisions.
Do you have other thoughts or beliefs that you hold strongly, even if others disagree with you?

Mostly just this.

I mean… I hold pretty strongly to what I’ve been saying. For months it’s been the same pattern with my sister’s appointments, the bills, people not calling me back. Other people can say it’s all mistakes, but I don’t think it is. I think information is being kept from me, and I’m being pushed out of decisions.
Do you think there is anything that could ever make you completely stop believing people are keeping information from you?

I don’t know.

Maybe if the pattern actually stopped for a while… if the appointments weren’t changed, the bills were right, people called me back and told me things directly. But as long as it keeps happening, I can’t just tell myself it isn’t real. It feels too much like they’re keeping me out.
